name: Grilled lake fish
summary: Small lake fish, clamped in bamboo and grilled over charcoal. VOV lists it first among the Pac Ngoi dishes. The Thái Nguyên portal calls the fish cá mương, a little bigger than a finger. VnExpress printed 10,000 VND for 3 skewers on 2 December 2014. A current price is Check on arrival.
origin: Pac Ngoi, on the lake. The Thái Nguyên provincial portal, 1 April 2026, and VnExpress, 2 December 2014 and the handbook updated 4 February 2025.
culture: VOV, on Vietnam Tourism's rural desk, lists cá nướng first at Pac Ngoi, with sour shrimp, măng vầu, upland sticky rice, and roast suckling pig. VOV's 2019 night-market note lists it again, with bamboo-tube rice and five-colour sticky rice.
texture: VnExpress, on 2 December 2014, calls the flesh fragrant, soft, fatty, and chewy. The Thái Nguyên portal calls it white and firm.
taste: VnExpress says the grilled fish is not fishy. The portal says the sweetness belongs to the lake. Neither account prints a drying step.
howToEat: Eat it hot. The handbook says it is better hot, with the rest of the house table. VnExpress says you can eat the meat, the bones, and the head.

The portal clamps the cleaned fish in bamboo and grills it until it is golden. VnExpress, in 2014, says the gall and the guts come out, then about 15 minutes on charcoal. The handbook says the fish is cleaned, seasoned, and grilled. A current price is Check on arrival.
The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Pac Ngoi, at the house. Bo Lu and Pac Ngoi are where VnExpress, in 2014, says the sour shrimp is sold, and the same shores are where the fish is eaten. Báo Xây dựng names grilled lake fish at Long Tong.
The 2019 weekend market at Pac Ngoi listed it. Whether that market still opens is Check on arrival.
